sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 24.2% a year from $1.70 billion in FY2016 to $12.0 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The FY2020 step change, revenue up 49.1% to $6.21 billion, came from the U.S. launch of TRIKAFTA in the fourth quarter of 2019 and KAFTRIO in the E.U. in the third quarter of 2020 [F5][D194][P51].
FY2024 broke the pattern: operating income fell to a $233 million loss on $4.6 billion of AIPR&D, including $4.4 billion for Alpine [F24][P11].
FY2025 recovered to $4.17 billion of operating income, but revenue growth slowed to 8.9% [F25][D446].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO contributed 13.1pp of FY2024's 11.7% revenue growth and only 0.7pp of FY2025's 8.9% [D528][D402][D531][D446].
ALYFTREK, launched in FY2025, added 7.6pp of growth and 7.0% of revenue [D590][D589].
FY2025 net product revenues rose $950.5 million, or 9%, on continued growth, with ALYFTREK sales absent a year earlier [P3][S39][S69].
Operating income grew faster than revenue over the window, at a 95.6% CAGR against 24.2% [F197][F196].
Diluted EPS rose to $15.32 in FY2025 from $13.89 in FY2023 while the diluted share count was flat at 258.0 million [F75][F73][X137].
The FY2025 operating margin of 34.8% sits above the 31.8% window median but below the 48.2% FY2022 high [F35][D663][D662].
The 36.9pp FY2025 margin recovery was mostly the absence of FY2024's AIPR&D, a 37.7pp residual effect [D452][D468].
Cost of revenue held at 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 as a lower overall royalty rate for CF medicines offset other costs [D425][P4].
SG&A rose 19.7% in FY2025, costing 1.3pp of margin, as commercial spend outgrew revenue [D456][D467].
The FY2024 net margin of -4.9% diverged from operating margin because the 315.5% effective tax rate reflected non-deductible Alpine AIPR&D [F54][D390][P5].
Operating cash flow was $3.63 billion in FY2025, primarily from $4.17 billion of income from operations [F85][F25][P1].
Free cash flow of $3.19 billion was 26.6% of revenue, below the 32.8% window median [F105][D431][D669].
Free cash flow covered only 0.81x of net income, against a 1.07x window median and a 1.11x peer median [D435][D675][D694].
Capex rose 47.0% to $438 million, 2.09x D&A and 3.6% of revenue [D447][F95][D436][D430].
Net cash of $12.3 billion equals 102.7% of revenue, in the 88th percentile of eight biopharma peers whose median is -50.7% [D439][D440][D691][D692].
Cash and investments rose 9.8% in FY2025, primarily on increased cash and marketable securities from product revenue [D460][P2].
Buybacks of $2.02 billion absorbed 63.2% of free cash flow in FY2025, yet the diluted share count was unchanged [D441][D442][D459].
The current ratio of 2.90x is below the 3.52x window median [F185][D678].
Days inventory outstanding rose 85 days to 373 in FY2025, up from 287 in FY2024 [D444][D397].
Inventory has grown faster than revenue for several years, tying up cash and raising write-down risk if demand shifts [D462][D446].
The effective tax rate fell 300.7pp to 14.9% in FY2025 from the distorted 315.5% FY2024 rate [D433][D390].
That swing is benign, reflecting FY2024's non-deductible Alpine charge rather than a change in the underlying tax position [P5].
If TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO growth stays near the 0.7% of FY2025, total revenue growth depends on ALYFTREK holding its 7.0% share [D530][D589].
A free-cash-flow-to-net-income ratio recovering toward the 1.07x window median would confirm the FY2025 cash rebound [D435][D675].
Days inventory outstanding falling back toward the 287 days of FY2024 would ease the working-capital drag [D444][D397].
